Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

[2026-22865] Rule — Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
Title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
Action: Final amendment; order; notification of partial denial of petition.
Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by Environmental Defense Fund et al. (petitioners), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, to remove the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. The petitioners provided data demonstrating that this additive induces cancer in laboratory animals. We are denying the remaining petition requests to remove ethylene dichloride, methylene chloride, and trichloroethylene from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, because any residue of the solvent would be an impurity in the color additive and such impurities are not subject to the Delaney Clause.

[2026-22866] Rule — Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration

Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by the International Association of Color Manufacturers (IACM or petitioner), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of abandonment, to remove the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The petitioner provided data demonstrating that these uses have been permanently abandoned. [2026-22903] Proposed Rule — Labor Department; Employment and Training Administration
Title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
Action: Proposed rule, request for comment.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State- level requirements for individuals to actively seek work.

Title: Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — CornerCare Pharmacy
Window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-13 · as of 2026-11-13 · 4 items

## Critical (3)

- **Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program** [Federal Register]
  - Check how Medicare’s negotiated drug prices and prescription coverage changes affect pharmacy payments, and update billing procedures to prevent payment errors.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-05 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement) · Areas: payers
  - 91 FR 72176 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22792/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program-and-medicare-prescription-drug-benefit-program
- **Rules of Practice and Procedure for Administrative Hearings Before the Office of Administrative Law Judges** [Federal Register]
  - Set up electronic filing for store workforce disputes heard by Department of Labor judges so CornerCare can submit required paperwork on time.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-09 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance) · Areas: privacy-people
  - 91 FR 70790 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22761/rules-of-practice-and-procedure-for-administrative-hearings-before-the-office-of-administrative-law
- **Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Oveporexton in Schedule IV** [Federal Register]
  - Review the proposed oveporexton restrictions and flag concerns for comment so stores can meet dispensing, inventory, and recordkeeping requirements if they stock it.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-14 (comment, FR field ✓) · Owner: Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations) · Areas: pharmacy-ops
  - 91 FR 72775 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23075/schedules-of-controlled-substances-placement-of-oveporexton-in-schedule-iv

## High (1)

- **Rules and Regulations, Series 8** [Federal Register]
  - Confirm what the National Labor Relations Board changed and update store procedures as needed so managers handle union elections and labor complaints correctly.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance) · Areas: privacy-people
  - 91 FR 72419 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22891/rules-and-regulations-series-8

votes.why: Plain English with a concrete step: review the payment impact and update billing procedures.
Makes no unsupported claims and avoids the forbidden December 2026 deadline and dispensing-fee claims.
Omits the maximum fair price cap plus dispensing fees, the negotiated price definition, and the January 1, 2029 start.
Plain, single concrete step: set up electronic filing for DOL ALJ disputes.
Consistent with the reason that electronic filing is generally required.
Understandable, with a concrete review-and-flag step.
Calls the restrictions 'proposed', which the rubric forbids; this is an effective interim final rule.
Omits the Schedule IV placement, the November 12 effective date and the December 14 comment deadline; mentions only some of the handling duties.
Plain English, with a concrete step to confirm the changes and update store procedures.
Acknowledges the change is unspecified and claims nothing beyond the reason.
Lucia’s first step is clear: check how the Medicare changes affect pharmacy payments before updating billing procedures.
The action reflects the potential effect on reimbursement without asserting an unsupported deadline, fee change, or dispensing duty.

It omits the Part D cap of the maximum fair price plus dispensing fees for selected drugs, the inclusion of sales tax and vaccine administration fees in the negotiated price, and the January 1, 2029 applicability date.
The action gives Sam a concrete next step in plain English: set up electronic filing for the specified disputes.
Setting up electronic filing follows from the stated general filing requirement for store workforce disputes before Department of Labor judges.
Priya can tell what to do next: review the oveporexton restrictions and flag any concerns.
Calling the restrictions proposed misstates the Schedule IV placement, which took effect under an interim final rule.

It mentions inventory and recordkeeping but omits the Schedule IV placement, the Orzeyful name, explicit security and prescription rules, interim-final status, and the effective and comment/hearing-request dates.
Sam’s immediate next step is clear: confirm what the Board changed before deciding whether store procedures need updating.
The action does not guess at the unspecified change and makes any procedure update conditional on what Sam finds.
Plain-English instruction giving the reimbursement owner a concrete review-and-update task.
Stays within the title and reason and avoids all prohibited claims in the rubric.
Omits the maximum fair price plus dispensing fee cap, sales tax and vaccine fee definition, and January 1, 2029 start date.
Uses plain language to assign one concrete step to set up electronic filing.
Directly reflects the electronic filing requirement for Department of Labor administrative law judge disputes stated in the reason.
Gives a plain-English, concrete next step to review the rule and flag comments.
Violates mustNotClaim by describing the interim final scheduling as proposed restrictions.
Misses Schedule IV placement (and brand name Orzeyful), security and prescription rules, interim final status, and the November 12 and December 14, 2026 dates.
Plainly tells the owner to check the unspecified rule change and update procedures if needed.
Accurately reflects that the NLRB notice lacks specifics and connects solely to the union and labor proceeding impacts in the reason.
